evidence: (a) Equivalent mechanism: DESIGN-NOTES.md:255-258 and CURRENT-DESIGN.md:34 require transcript identity, processed-through coverage, output references, and durable completion, but specify no rule for selecting/combining concurrent results; DESIGN-NOTES.md:259 explicitly leaves out-of-order handling open. (b) No accepted tradeoff permits regression in represented coverage: delegated semantic summarization (CURRENT-DESIGN.md:10) and best-effort manual Herdr observation (CURRENT-DESIGN.md:16) address different boundaries. (c) Mechanical transcript processing/indexing is expressly in scope (CURRENT-DESIGN.md:10,32-34). (d) A later-arriving result for an earlier transcript portion could be exposed as the latest usable summary without the resumed portion, impairing the stated recovery/continuity goal (HERDR-GRAPH-VISION.md:37,139). Narrowing: the spec does not promise a single current pointer or allow overwriting a shared artifact; those are illustrative failure paths, not established behavior. The material missing rule is how graph represents usable coverage when results complete out of order. This is an acknowledged design gap, not an implementation claim.
